items.text: Recursive self-improving, a field's expression, holds one shared idea, an improving returning into the system producing further improvings, and parts at how far that return reaches, what a self is and whether it goes on with no end. A stronger saying, a synthesis and no agreed field definition: a system improves its own improving process and goes on improving itself with that improved process. Three qualify an observed sequence, each is-or-is-not: the system takes part in changing its own improving process; the changed process is an improving by the criterion its application holds; and the improved process takes part in a next self-improving. A failed change, retained or renamed, is no improving. Repeating alone, a changed program alone or a better task output alone shows neither relation, and an unchanged optimizer bettering its outputs improves no optimizer; recursion here is no program calling itself. Each application holds its own criterion of improving, no one numerical objective for all, and identifies its continuing system and its improving process; a sequence of successor versions counted as a self is not by that a same-existing self. Unlimited, exponentially accelerating or universal improving is a further claim, said apart. A field's accounts part along these lines: a broad use asks no rewriting of each component or of the whole improving algorithm; improving a performance and improving a capacity for further improving are two, and a self's identity across replaced code stands open there; one formal model has each program generating its successor, each successor improving by one same goal, its sequence with no end; and one engineering case applies a code-improving program to its own code and its improved versions to further optimizing, the language model it calls fixed, a bounded system's improving and not the whole system's.
